scope: Accept the PHPStan-only reclassification as an excluded documented configuration-scope divergence, not a clean result or proof of runtime safety.

findings.finding: The correction has affirmative documentation and source support. It is not justified merely by the existence of an optional flag or by silence. PHPStan explicitly gives array-key a lenient dialect meaning that differs from plain int|string.

The contract describes unsupported as a rule not implemented by design, whereas this check is implemented but disabled in the measured configuration. The reason explicitly discloses this distinction and the existing docblock-return-covariance case already uses the same configuration-scope convention. Accept under that established convention; do not publish this as missing PHPStan capability.

The documentation's checkBenevolentUnionTypes example concerns scalar array-key arguments, not this nested array key. The pinned ArrayType normalization and the checkImplicitMixed differential probe supply the otherwise missing concrete link. The two flags must not be conflated.

evidence.observation: Read both. Ground truth must remain independent of analyzer output, and corrections require justification rather than score-driven predicate relaxation. The current diff preserves runtime ground truth, fixture and Psalm/Mago required predicates, and changes PHPStan expectation plus explanatory notes/provenance. git diff --name-only listed only this case.json during review.

Official documentation says: PHPStan defines benevolent union types, such as array-key. Benevolent unions aren't checked strictly even at the highest level. Its example marks both requireInt($value1) and requireString($value1) as No error for array-key, while the corresponding int|string calls are Error. checkBenevolentUnionTypes defaults false and requires level 7 or higher.

Verified HEAD and no local diff in inspected source files. src/PhpDoc/TypeNodeResolver.php:283-284 maps array-key to new BenevolentUnionType([new IntegerType(), new StringType()]). src/Type/ArrayType.php:75-85 converts this benevolent key to new MixedType(), and converts StrictMixedType back to a plain string/int union. src/Rules/RuleLevelHelper.php:85-118 traverses nested types and converts implicit mixed only when checkImplicitMixed is true. conf/config.neon:73 sets it false; level9 sets checkExplicitMixed true, not checkImplicitMixed; level10 enables checkImplicitMixed.

Read both complete probe records. False exits 0 with zero diagnostics; True exits 1 with one argument.type at repro.php:26, expecting array<string, int>, array<int> given. Both use /bench/tools/bin/phpstan.phar, level 9, --debug and the unchanged source directory. The only probe config parameter is checkImplicitMixed: true.

Verified PHP 8.3.35 and PHPStan 2.3.1. Independently repeated php tools/bin/phpstan.phar analyse --no-progress --error-format=json --level=9 --debug cases/arrays/array-key-for-string-key/src, then the same command with -c .amp/in/key-scope.neon. Reproduced zero diagnostics and exactly one argument.type at line 26 respectively. No fixture changes were made.

Runtime proof exited 0 and reported strtoupper(): Argument #1 ($string) must be of type string, int given. Read fixture and runtime controls. This preserves the concrete unsafe program independently of the configured diagnostic promise.

Existing case excludes deliberately suppressed maybe-compatible PHPDoc signature checking and explicitly says the rule exists. Official documentation confirms that option defaults false. This is consistent with the correction's configuration-aware interpretation, though the mechanism differs.

contradictory_evidence: The runtime defect is real and a soundness-only benchmark could legitimately record default-configuration silence as a miss. This acceptance applies to the repository's documented-promise/configuration-scope benchmark convention, not an assertion that default PHPStan catches the defect.

The unchanged ground_truth statement calls array-key int|string and says a diagnostic belongs on the call. That is correct for the neutral key-set/runtime contract, but not a statement that PHPStan promises strict alias equivalence. The per-tool reason and notes explicitly disclose the dialect exception.

Enabling a stricter option alone would not justify exclusion. Here affirmative array-key leniency documentation, the pinned normalization mechanism and the same-fixture differential probe jointly justify it.

The docs say benevolent unions remain lenient even at the highest level, while level10's implicit-mixed check catches this fixture. This is not a contradiction in the tested mechanism: ArrayType has already normalized the benevolent key into implicit mixed, so the nested key is governed by the mixed setting.
